mapping_rule: Every v5/v6 predicate is either present_in_prose or moved_to_debt. Credentials, secondary endpoints, and transfer boundaries may move; no moved item is treated as discharged until its manuscript destination is frozen.

claims.predicate: Direct-answer validation can mark an edit successful without establishing its behavior once the model reasons.
Each ROME edit on CounterFact is compared at zero thinking and after a natural chain across six fixed checkpoints from two DeepSeek-R1-distill families.
At each family's largest tested checkpoint, within-edit success drops 0.106 and 0.107; the paired design is established in S2.
On Qwen-32B, the old answer resurfaces in 19.3% of zero-thinking successes and displaces the new answer in 9.2%.
The Qwen-32B erosion is edit-specific relative to null-compatible old-answer drift in the unedited base.
A canned thought does not reproduce the Qwen-32B erosion.
The erosion persists across three fixed sampling seeds.
In examined Qwen-32B reversions, the edited association remains detectable at a cloze probe.
A separate route analysis identifies visible in-chain routes that motivate a chain-routing hypothesis.
A think-span-only old-answer first-token intervention leaves answer logits untouched and tests a chain-local control point.
The signed, dose-graded intervention offsets the observed loss in edit success.
The arm-wise resurfacing rate falls from 19.3% without suppression to 8.5% with suppression.
Placebo and same-relation controls have near-null answer-level effects; their endpoint-level limitations remain a manuscript debt.
The ROME strict endpoint improves against controls but not detectably against no suppression.
Positive 14B and MEMIT edit-success transfer coexists with inconclusive MEMIT strict transfer and a null-compatible fresh-N erosion check.
Edit evaluation needs a reasoning-time stress test, and the failure admits a chain-local causal control point.
The complete-case paired loose-reversion change is −0.102 with uncertainty excluding zero.
